sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority: code page for ygm and Change Request 2025-042 (Devin O'Bannon, SIL Global; pending) 'Update language name [ygm] Yagomi to Tandɨ; retain the name Yagomi', LCA-revised to reference name 'Tanda'
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; settles identity: quotes Carter et al. 2023:14-15 (Suter p.c.: Tandɨ = Z'graggen's Yagomi) and van den Berg 2020 ('The language is called Tanda, pronounced [tandə]').

sources.citation: Carter, Jed, Beautlyn Eliab, Karl Kama, Roger Maikei, Devin O'Bannon & Napa Yanderave. 2023. Survey Report for Uma (Ronji) [roe], Tandɨ (Yagomi) [ygm], Muratayak [asx], Degenang (Degenan) [dge], and Forak [frq] Languages. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2023-003. Dallas: SIL International. 71 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing: re-checked 2026-09-17, the strings stress/accent/tone/tonal/prosod/syllab/pitch/intonation and the IPA marks ˈ ˌ occur zero times in the text layer. Sec. 2.1.4 (p. 10): 120-item SIL-PNG list 'transcribed using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) and.. digitally recorded'; App. D Table 37 (pp. 55-64) Tandɨ column in IPA without stress marking; sec. 1.2.2/1.2.6 (pp. 5-6): prior research on Yagomi = Z'graggen 1975 only; sec. 3.1.1.2 (pp. 15-16): Tandɨ = Yagomi (Suter p.c.), 20-30 elderly speakers, EGIDS 8a.

sources.citation: SIL Global publications entry 95956 for Carter et al. 2023 (abstract, TOC, PDF link)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic: abstract and table of contents (Introduction, Methodology, Language and dialect boundaries, Language vitality, Conclusions, Appendices); no phonology chapter.

sources.citation: van den Berg, René. 2020. New highly endangered language discovered in PNG. Post to the PapuanLanguages discussion list (ANU), 17 March 2020 (Glottolog dates it '2010', a typo)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or prosody. Name 'Tanda, pronounced [tandə]'; secret clan language of ~10 families in Yagomi village; 'The SIL team collected a 170-item wordlist (with recordings)'; 22 words given in IPA (dɔman 'head', mɛruan 'hair', tɛndɔmna 'nose', dalaŋ 'eye', walik 'woman', umgak 'man'..) with no stress marks.

sources.citation: Suter, Edgar (University of Cologne). Unpublished comparative Finisterre/Warup files including the 2020 Tandɨ vs. Z'graggen Yagomi comparison reported as p.c. in Carter et al. 2023 and ISO 639-3 CR 2025-042

sources.note: Suter is the only linguist known to have analysed the Tandɨ data; any phonological notes (incl. accent) would be here.

sources.citation: SIL-PNG Survey Office (Ukarumpa): February 2020 Tandɨ (Yagomi village) 120/170-item SIL-PNG wordlist field transcriptions and digital audio recordings collected by the Carter et al. survey team (Carter et al. 2023 sec. 2.1.4, p. 10; van den Berg 2020)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only recordings of the language in existence; stress placement could be heard or measured directly. The printed list omits stress marks but the field sheets or audio may not. SIL ('unlikely to do further work') offered the data to the PapuanLanguages list in 2020 (van den Berg 2020: 'please let me know and I can provide more information').

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. ca. 1971-1973. Unpublished field wordlist of A7 Yagomi (Warup family), Madang survey elicitation list; Z'graggen papers / Anthropos Institute. Consulted by Edgar Suter (p.c. in Carter et al. 2023 sec. 3.1.1.2)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only other primary record of the language; never printed (PL B-41 is a checklist and PL D-30 covers the Rai Coast stock, not the Finisterre languages). Z'graggen's field transcriptions sometimes carry stress marks dropped in publication.
